summary.tldr: Harmonizes federal laws with Quebec civil law and updates related rules for banks, property, information, evidence, and several other statutes.
what_it_does: Rewrites the main federal financial institution laws to add Quebec civil law terms, update definitions, change proxy rules, and revise rules for transfers, lending, leasing, and holding certain roles.
Updates many federal laws to use civil law and common law terms in both language versions, including rules on immovables, hypothecs, fiduciaries, mandataries, and related-party contracts.
Changes access to information, privacy, official languages, and disclosure laws to expand good-faith protection for certain commissioners and to cover more property transactions.
Updates other laws on evidence, Crown property, food and product enforcement, dry docks subsidies, escheats, human rights, conflict of interest, and cultural property redeterminations.
summary.background: This is the fourth bill in a series linked to the Civil Code of Québec, which came into force in 1994. It amends 52 statutes.
